correctness.rationale: For every prime power q, the Frobenius-factorized tangent polynomial has exactly eight possible exponents. Vanishing of its qth coefficient is equivalent, via the hyperplane dual and d(q-1)=q^3-1, to projective F_{q^3}-rationality. At nonboundary rational points the q+1 coefficient equals -A_0A_1/A_2 and is nonzero; at boundary points the tangent restricts to a dth power. Norm fibres yield exactly (q-2)d^2 and 3d points. For generic orders (0,1,q), adapted local Hasse–Wronskians have leading coefficients binom(q+1,q)=binom(d,q)=1 mod p, verifying ramification weights 1 and d-q, and their global degree matches (q+1)(2g-2)+3d. The independently constructed finite-field program was executed successfully on GF(8), GF(27), GF(64), GF(125), and q=2 over GF(64), including 98 nonflex points. No sampling is taken as the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Computing an entire ramification divisor of a natural nonclassical plane embedding is a structurally motivated exact invariant, not merely the elementary F_{q^3}-point count. The theorem explains all exceptional tangent contacts via the norm map, separates high-contact coordinate points from ordinary q-flexes, and gives exact scheme multiplicities and a global Plücker/Stöhr–Voloch consistency check. The d-contact stratum differs sharply from a generic Komeda member and has a geometric reason. It is an interpretable infinite-family classification suitable for further study of osculating geometry and dual behavior.
